thread:
alex: Hey team — first day here. macbook M1, completed Okta SSO + WireGuard profile from the portal. I can reach public sites but https://redwood.internal/docs/vpc-onboard times out. Browser shows DNS error. Anyone hit this with split-tunnel profiles?
jamie: welcome! :wave: did the portal include the internal DNS option? sometimes the profile omits the 10.x/172.16.x routes. which client did you use (WireGuard app or system config)?
alex: WireGuard app from the portal. I checked routes:
```
$ netstat -rn | grep 10
# nothing returned for 10.0.0.0/8
```
so no internal route. dig returns NXDOMAIN for internal host.
samira: ok that points at missing routes and DNS. on macs try `scutil --dns` to inspect resolver info. you can temporarily add a route for testing: `sudo route -n add -net 10.0.0.0/8 <wg_peer_ip>` (replace with the WireGuard peer/gateway). also `dig @172.16.0.10 redwood.internal` to query internal DNS directly.
alex: scutil shows no search domains and no 172.16.0.10 resolver. dig @172.16.0.10 returns answers when I run from my home network, but not after connecting — weird.
infra-bot: Policy check: user alex missing tag 'internal-dns'. To access internal DNS and route provisioning, run `infra request-access --tag internal-dns` or have infra add the tag.
jamie: @marta can you check tags for alex? sometimes the onboarding automation missed the DNS role.
marta: checking... looks like onboarding job skipped the DNS tag. adding `internal-dns` now and pushing updated WireGuard profile. FYI M1 macs occasionally keep stale resolver state; after I push the profile please do: 1) disconnect VPN, 2) kill mDNSResponder `sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder`, 3) reconnect. Also you can enable "Push DNS" toggle in the portal to ensure domains are applied.
alex: got the update, followed steps. `scutil --dns` now shows 172.16.0.10 and search domain `redwood.internal`. dig resolves and I can open the docs page. Thank you! Quick question: do I need bastion access for the docs UI or only SSH targets?
samira: docs UI sits in a private subnet accessible via internal routes/DNS — bastion is only for SSH into private EC2 instances. For web UI you just need the internal-dns tag and route.
alex: awesome, all set. Appreciate the quick help :tada:
